initialPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one 4-by-4 texture variation atlas for the existing hand-painted dungeon game.
Reference image 1 is the ORIGINAL game's style/mood reference. Reference image 2 is the CURRENT approved texture palette, not a layout to reproduce. Match their cool dark desaturated slate-blue hues, readable hand-painted fantasy game treatment and upper-left lighting. This is an expanded material library, not a new room picture.

Create ONE square image, exactly sixteen equal square swatches in a precise four-column, four-row grid. Each swatch is a full-bleed close-up of one uninterrupted STONE SURFACE. There must be no brick borders, grout grid, rectangular frame, raised tile, bevel around swatch edges, masonry arrangement, 3D perspective, labels or text. The grid division is only where the sixteen different surface paintings meet. Each swatch uses the SAME restrained slate/indigo palette and similar medium-dark value; variants should mix as stones in one dungeon without looking like different materials or different colors.

Rows 1 and 2 (8 wall surfaces):
1 broad irregular painted planes with two shallow weathered chips,
2 layered stone planes with a small worn depression,
3 softer rounded wear and asymmetrical cloudy stone patches,
4 quiet nearly intact stone with different irregular planes,
5 sparse fine dark organic fracture with worn edges, never a straight branching symbol,
6 uneven mineral strata and one chipped area,
7 a localized recessed natural fissure with a SMALL dim violet light deep within it, occupying at most 8% of swatch, no neon traced line,
8 a different compact patch of purple corruption inside a dark crevice at a different position, occupying at most 8%.
Make every wall swatch genuinely independently composed, no copied diagonal motif, no identical chip position, no mosaic of uniform triangular facets.

Rows 3 and 4 (8 floor surfaces):
9 calm worn slate with broad soft patches,
10 two shallow chips and a subtly abraded area,
11 a tiny natural hairline crack offset from center,
12 broad rubbed smooth stone with irregular quiet shading,
13 sparse shallow pits grouped asymmetrically,
14 low-contrast layered stone wear,
15 a short weathered fracture and one small chip in different positions,
16 faint old scraped surface markings blended into the stone, no symbols.
The floors are quieter than the walls, still noticeably distinct from each other. No bright floor glowing motifs, no brown/green moss, no dirt clumps or objects.

Keep a sophisticated painted cartoon game look: broad organic brush shapes, subtle local texture, controlled small detail, crisp selective chips with soft color transitions. Avoid photographic rock grain, noisy microtexture, repeating herringbone/triangles, sterile smooth vector gradients, uniform diagonal streaks and simple violet line doodles. Opaque material sheet. No transparent background, no characters, no torches, no wood, no metal, no UI.
refinementPrompt:
Edit the supplied 4x4 stone-surface texture atlas, preserving exactly the 16-square grid and the existing dark desaturated slate-blue palette and overall values. It is material art for a stylized painted dungeon, not stone tiles with borders.
The first version has the same sweeping BOTTOM-LEFT to TOP-RIGHT diagonal bands in nearly every swatch. REMOVE this repeated directional pattern. Make the surfaces independently composed and mostly NON-DIRECTIONAL, with broad soft-edged irregular patches, rounder subtle planes, worn areas and localized chips. Do not just rotate the same surface. Keep the subtle game-painted look, no photographic noise.
Top 8 squares are walls. Six are neutral with different wear: calm patches, a shallow rounded depression, a small chipped edge-like area inside the swatch, short weathered fractures, scattered small pits, and soft mineral patches. The last two have localized violet corruption INSIDE small natural recesses, with the glow small and sparse, not giant black branching trenches or purple line symbols.
Bottom 8 squares are floors. Make them low-contrast worn stone, eight distinctly different irregular arrangements: calm mottling, small shallow nicks, a compact weathered crack, a rubbed smooth area, a few faint pits, cloudy mineral variation, one short chipped fracture and a faint worn patch. Keep each floor quiet enough for characters. No long aligned scratches, no broad repeated diagonal strata, no chevrons. Keep floor values close to current atlas.
Preserve no text, no labels, no frame around each square, no brick seams inside the squares, no stones drawn as isolated blocks, no perspective. Each square is just full-bleed material. More organic painterly shapes and meaningful variation without making it detailed or realistic.
note: First atlas retained too much repeated diagonal direction. Second atlas looked too granular in assembly. Third atlas restores broad quiet painted shapes. User then identified small floor slab size as a likely main cause: floor-size-comparison.png compares 6, 3 and 2 rows per 1x1 cell with the same proposed material pool. User approved size C on 2026-10-23. Its geometry is installed with the existing approved production materials. This new material atlas remains a proposal.
